items.title: Deepseek FREE Coder Setup: So, this is ACTUALLY USABLE!!
items.summary:
In this video, I'll be showing you four different ways to use DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 for free, including Cline, OpenCode, Freebuff, and NVIDIA NIM. We'll also look at the caveats around free access, data usage, ads, and which option makes the most sense depending on your workflow.

--
Key Takeaways:

🚀 DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 is now available for free through multiple coding tools.  
🧠 Cline offers the updated DeepSeek V4 Flash model for free inside its coding agent workflow.  
🛠️ OpenCode has added DeepSeek V4 Flash Free through OpenCode Zen for a limited time.  
🔥 Freebuff gives access to DeepSeek V4 Pro, the larger 1.6 trillion-parameter model, for free.  
⚠️ Freebuff is free because it uses ads and may use your data for ad personalization and AI training.  
🔑 NVIDIA NIM provides free API access to DeepSeek models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.  
🔒 The biggest caveat with all free options is data privacy, so avoid using confidential code or private projects.  
👍 Overall, Deep

items.transcript: [music] Hi, welcome to another video. So, we've been covering the new DeepSseek V4 Flash0731 update a lot recently. I tested it on my bench where it did really well and I showed you the one command code setup and the new ReasonX agent. Those videos will be linked below. But a lot of you in the comments asked the obvious question, can I use Deepseek for free? And the answer right now is yes, actually in multiple ways. Because ever since the 0731 update dropped, basically every coding tool has been racing to add it. And a bunch of them are offering it completely free. So in this video, I'll show you four ways to use DeepSeek for free, including one that gives you the big V4 Pro model for free with some caveats that we'll talk about. So let's get right into it. The first option is Scle. Klein announced that they're making the updated Deepseek V40731 free in Klein. And their wording here is actually pretty strong. They said this is the first flash model they found that performs at soda levels. And when the Klein team says that, it means something because they test a lot of models in their harness. The setup is super simple. Run npmi-gl to install the CLI. Then open it. Type / settings. Go to the client provider and select deepsee-v4-lash. That's it. You're now running the new 0731 model through client's provider for free with their whole plan and act workflow on top. And Klein is also the one that caught this update early. By the way, they noticed that Deepseek silently updated their change log with the new V4 Flash before the official announcement even landed with that terminal bench score jumping 25.8 points from the April preview to 82.7. So, they've been on top of this model from hour one. The second option is Open Code. Open Code announced that the new Deepseek V4 Flash is now available in Open Code Go and also on the free tier. and they said the initial reactions are that it's a big improvement over preview which matches what I saw on my bench too. The way this works is through open code zen which is their model gateway. You sign in, grab an API key and then run the /models command inside open code to see the list. In there you'll find v4 flash free. Their docs say it's available for free for a limited time and that they use this period to gather feedback and that collected data may be used to improve the model. So the caveat here is clear. It's free for a limited time and your usage data can be used for training for personal projects and learning that trade is probably fine. For anything confidential obviously don't. The third option is the wild one and that is freebuff. Freebuff is a completely free CLI coding agent from James Grugget who is the codebuff founder and it's built on the codebuff agent framework. And this one doesn't just give you flash, it gives you deepsee v4 pro, the big 1.6 trillion parameter model for free. It also has other models like Kimmy, Miniax, and GLM in the lineup depending on the tier. Install is just npm, I-G, freebuff. No subscription, no configuration. You just start it in your project. It even comes with nine specialized sub aents and a nice/in/plimp implement/re workflow built in. Now, how is this free? Well, you're paying with two things. First, ads. There are small textonly ads from developer focused sponsors that show up between agent turns. And second, data. Their own policy says that prompts and messages may be analyzed to personalize ads and the features marked as may use data for AI training can use your submissions to train and improve AI models. So let me be really clear about this one. Freebuff is genuinely free and genuinely useful and honestly the ads in the terminal thing is a pretty creative business model but you are the product here. Your prompts can be used for ads personalization and model training. So use it for learning side projects and open source stuff. Do not paste your company's codebase into it. Also, one more limit. In unsupported countries or behind a VPN, it runs in a limited mode with Deepseek V4 flash only and six 1-hour sessions per day, which to be fair is still free. And the fourth option is Nvidia Nim, which I covered in detail in a previous video. Through the NVIDIA developer program, you can get free API access to Deepseek models on build.envidia.com with an OpenAI compatible endpoint that you can plug into basically any tool. The full setup is in that video which is linked below. One thing I'd say here is I haven't confirmed whether Nvidia's endpoint has been updated to the new 0731 version yet. So check the model page before assuming you're getting the new flash there since DeepSeek kept the same model ID. Hosts should be able to swap it in quietly, but different hosts update at different speeds. So which one should you actually use? If you want the new V4 flash0731 in a proper harness with zero friction, I'd go with Klein. It's the actual updated model confirmed by them in one of the most mature open- source coding agents. If you're already an open code user, the free tier option there is a no-brainer while it lasts. If you want the big V4 Pro model for free and you're okay with ads and data collection, FreeBuff is honestly kind of amazing for students. A 1.6 trillion parameter frontier class model for $0 is not something we had even a year ago. And if you want a raw API key for your own scripts and custom agents, NVIDIA NIM is the route. Just remember the golden rule with all of these. When something this expensive is free, you're usually paying with your data. Every single one of these options has some version of that trade, whether it's limited time feedback gathering, training data collection, or ad personalization. For learning and personal projects, take the free stuff and enjoy it. For serious or confidential work, pay the $1 for command code, or use the official API directly and keep your data out of the training pipelines. But still, think about where we are. The model that beat GLM 5.2 on Agentic Benchmarks that set a record on My Bench's hardest question is now available for free in at least three different coding agents within days of its release. Ever since the big lab started tightening limits and raising prices, Deep Seek keeps dragging the whole market in the opposite direction. And for us, that's just great. Overall, it's pretty cool. Anyway, let me know your thoughts in the comments. If you like this video, [music] consider donating through the Superthanks option or becoming a member by clicking the join button. Also, give this [music] video a thumbs up and subscribe to my channel. I'll see you in the next one. Until then, bye. >> [music]
